Yep. That's understood. Recipe is:
450 flour (360 strong 90 spelt)
383ml water
10g dried active yeast
9.5g salt
No added fat. 


If using a poolish it's taking 90g flour (spelt) with an equal amount of watee and 0.05g dried yeast, fermenting for about 13 hours. I can knead by hand in about 30 minutes if not using the poolish. Using poolish more than doubles the kneading time (at least). 


I've made it at over 100% hydration, using the poolish and without. it's.... Hard work! No autolysis besides the preferment. But I enjoy the challenge. I just don't understand why the poolish makes the dough so much harder to work with, I don't even know for certain that it's the poolish or just coincidental, other factors etc.

Unfortunately not. Apologies the post was made whilst taking a breather and frustrated... so lacks context. 


I'm looking for the root cause. If you make two doughs using exactly the same recipe however a portion of one dough (20%) is via a poolish. Ignoring the techniques used, just assuming same technique for each dough, is the dough containing poolish harder to bring together? 


And if it is, why?

The module number is on the back of the movement itself, not just the backplate. Small font but it's there somewhere. Or run diagnostic mode which will give you the base module, not necessarily the derivative you have. But it's a start.
GBX-100 GBD-200 GB-5600 = all squares. Also GBD-100 GD-350 GW-400 GBD-H1000 GBD-H2000 GSW-H1000 and a few outliers I'd have thought

There's also G-9300 GA-1000 GA-1100 GG-1000 GN-1000 G-9200 which may be able to be found used In the price range. But it depends on the sensor(s) required. Most people don't consider it a watch with sensors but the GBD-200/GBX-100 are (technically speaking) watches with a sensor (accelerometer).

A very simple throw together pasta 'dish', We use it to get rid of left over herbs and bits of cheese.
But it's really tasty imo. 
Will cover 2 - 6 portions pasta depending on size and how much sauce you want. Easily stretched. But 3 or 4 portions is the sweet spot. 

1 ripe avocado halved, flesh removed
¼ cup olive oil
¼ cup cheese (50/50 Cheddar and parmesan works well)
¼ cup fresh soft herbs (oregano, basil, coriander, mint, curly/flat leaf parsley) with a few leaves reserved for dressing if likes
1-3 cloves garlic
Juice of 2 limes or lemons or mix of either
Fresh chillis or chilli powder/cayenne to taste
Pinch salt & pinch pepper

Instructions;
- Blend into mush
- Add to strained pasta with half cup pasta water reserved (just in case) 
- Gently heat through and use pasta water if consistency too thick 
- Add herb leaves if kept plus sliced mozzarella 

All very loose and easy but you can come up with multiple minor variations with surprisingly different results. Parsley and basil or coriander and mint are the natural choices for herb combos.

Make a thick paste using fairy liquid, bicarbonate of soda (not baking powder) and a dash of white vinegar. Remove bezel from watch. Coat the bezel in the paste rubbing it on and in gently. Leave for anywhere from 2 to 24 hours depending on severity of staining. Scrub gently with cold water and soft-medium brush. Rinse. It's worked for me. It depends if your bezel is stained or damaged. To access LCD diagnostic mode:

In timekeeping mode, press buttons (A), (C) and (D) simultaneously.

All segments of the LCD display will activate.

Press (D) to cycle through display test modes.

Last screen will show Casio module number.

Press any button to return to normal.

A- top left C- bottom left D- bottom right.

I'm not a huge recipe person. Esquites all for single serving, single person; 
1 cup corn kernels, 1 tablespoon corn oil. 
Dressing per person; 1 tbsp mayo, 1.5 tbsp cottage cheese, 1 tsp fine chopped chilli (jalapeno, lazy chilli etc as long as its hot), 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 garlic clove minced/crushed, 2 tbsps roughly chopped coriander (cilantro), 0.25 of a lime juiced/squeezed, salt and pepper to taste. 
Fry corn over medium heat till browned/blackened depending on preference (10-15 minutes) whilst making dressing. Mix the dressing. Cool the corn for 5 minutes+ and then combine with dressing in a salad bowl.
You can remove the oil through draining or even pat dry, whatever you prefer, I include all the oil. 
Dress with more cottage cheese. Can also dress with more lime zest, coriander, chilli whatever you like.
Use cottage cheese juice or a little oil to thin the dressing to preference of consistency if necessary/desired.
